about: How the foldouts fold, and which faces touch when the book is closed, as Lisa Fagin Davis described them in a comment on the Voynich Viewer thread on the Voynich Ninja forum (src, a key of orders.json's sources). Edit by hand. Keyed by sheet, and true only for the sheet folded as it is bound today: in an order that sews or turns it differently, 3D works its contacts out and marks them inferred. 'folds': every fold other than the spine, keyed 'a|b' by the picture ids of the two panels it joins, or by one panel's id for the extra crease inside that panel; 'in' brings the inside faces of the sheet together, 'out' the outside faces. A fold not listed folds in, as the viewer always assumed. 'touch': pairs of faces that lie against each other inside a folded leaf. 'shows': per leaf, the faces a folded leaf shows on its inside, so what the page facing it touches. Faces are named as the viewer names them; '(part)' where she says only part of a face touches, and on the two pieces of a panel the viewer creases in two. 'touch': 'all' says every contact the viewer works out for the sheet is right. A contact the record does not cover stays inferred. 'creases': where the extra crease in a panel lies, as a fraction of the panel's width from the fold it hangs from, measured on the Yale photographs she pointed to (5 Oct 2026). 'drawn': per leaf, its panels in hinge order with where each runs from and to (0 the spine, 100 the fore-edge), for the drawings on the Info page; schematic, not measured.
